title: Merge every repository in a tackle-tasks worktree back to its source branch
description:
implement ~/.claude/plans/submodule-merge-tackle-tasks.md

Problem: a worktree's submodules are separate clones whose git directories live at <main>/.git/worktrees/<name>/modules/<submodule>, with no shared object storage. mergeTaskWorktrees.ts merges only the parent branch and then calls removeWorktreeAndBranch -> `git worktree remove --force`, which deletes that directory and every submodule commit in it. The merged parent gitlink is left pointing at a commit that exists nowhere. This has already destroyed work.

Model to implement: a worktree is a set of repositories (parent plus every submodule at any depth) and the rule is uniform across all of them. Setup: the worktree is cut from the parent's current branch, and every repository in it gets a branch named task-group-N, each submodule starting at the commit the main repo's submodule was on. Teardown: every repository merges its task-group-N branch back into the branch it was spawned from. Nothing is removed.

Decisions already made: nothing is ever deleted (no worktree removal, no branch deletion); a repository on a detached HEAD refuses the run at prepare time before any worker spawns; each repository's source branch is recorded at prepare time rather than read from the `branch =` field in .gitmodules; submodules merge before the parent so the parent's gitlink conflict resolves to the already-merged submodule commit; the merge reads each worktree submodule's actual current branch instead of assuming the task-group-N name, so worktrees created before this change still merge.

Work: (1) new scripts/repositoryBranches.ts exporting currentBranchName, submodulePaths (recursive, via `git submodule --quiet foreach --recursive 'echo $displaypath'`), collectRepositorySources (throws once naming every detached repository), and createBranchInEveryRepository. prepareTasks.ts is near the 250-line cap, which is why this is a separate module. (2) WorkflowArguments gains repositorySources: {path, sourceBranch}[] -- path "" is the parent. buildWorkflowArguments calls collectRepositorySources first so a detached repo aborts before any worktree is created. createWorktreeForGroup creates the group branch in the parent and every submodule after the existing submodule init, tolerating an already-existing branch since the function is idempotent. (3) mergeTaskWorktrees.ts gains mergeSubmoduleBranchIntoRepo (fetch `<branch>:refs/heads/<groupBranch>` from the worktree submodule into the main submodule -- the refspec's second half creates the permanent branch name as part of the fetch, so commits survive whatever the merge does -- then checkout the source branch and merge --no-ff, aborting on conflict) and resolveGitlinkConflicts (all conflicted paths are submodule paths -> git add each and commit --no-edit; any non-submodule path -> abort and report, existing behavior). runAsCli merges submodules deepest-first, then the parent, and no longer calls removeWorktreeAndBranch; it reports worktree paths and branch names instead. A submodule conflict marks the whole group conflicted and skips the parent merge. MergeOutcome gains submoduleConflicts.

Tests (RED first): new tests/repositoryBranches.test.ts covering the parent-plus-submodule listing, the throw naming every detached repository, and branch creation across all repositories; prepareTasks tests for every submodule landing on the group branch, for buildWorkflowArguments refusing a detached submodule without creating any worktree directory, and for recorded source branches; merge tests for work landing on the source branch, for the group branch surviving a conflict (the data-loss regression test), for the worktree and branch still existing after a successful runAsCli merge, and for gitlink-only conflict auto-resolution versus a real file conflict aborting. Fixtures can reuse the GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL="file" approach already in tests/prepareTasks.test.ts.

Verification: node --test 'tests/*.test.ts' all green; re-add the removeWorktreeAndBranch call and confirm the worktree-survives test fails; drop the `:refs/heads/<groupBranch>` half of the fetch refspec and confirm the conflict-survival test fails; end-to-end on a scratch repo with parent and submodule both on develop.

Known consequences to accept: runs are blocked in any repo where a submodule sits on a detached HEAD, and worktrees now accumulate indefinitely since no cleanup path remains.
closureNote: Implemented in c57411f and merged as c56cea4: every repository in a worktree now gets a task-group-N branch at prepare time and merges back into its recorded source branch at teardown, the removeWorktreeAndBranch call was dropped from runAsCli so nothing is deleted, and mergeSubmoduleBranchIntoRepo fetches the worktree submodule branch into the main submodule before merging so commits survive a conflict.

title: Versioned repository manifest with RepositoryOccurrence records
description:
Phase 1 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign.

Create scripts/repositoryManifest.ts: a versioned run manifest that replaces the flat repository-path model with an occurrence graph. Define a RepositoryOccurrence record holding a stable occurrence ID, the root-relative checkout path, the explicit parent occurrence ID, the path within the immediate parent, the recorded gitlink OID, depth, origin URL, base branch and base OID, the operation branch name, child occurrence IDs, and test state. Add a manifest version constant, read/write helpers, and a validator.

Parentage is always an explicit edge. Nothing in this module may derive a parent with dirname(), path-segment removal, or slash counting.

New module only: do not wire it into scripts/prepareTasks.ts, scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts, or skills/tackle-tasks/tackle-tasks.workflow.js. Production stays on the existing flat path until the Phase 4 cutover task.

Tests: round-trip serialization preserves every field; the validator rejects dangling parent IDs, duplicate occurrence IDs, and depth values inconsistent with the parent chain; a manifest describing jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external/tmux_lib records its parent as the jfred/jfredToolsPlugin occurrence, never a synthetic jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external entry.
closureNote: Implemented scripts/repositoryManifest.ts with the versioned RepositoryOccurrence graph, manifest version constant, read/write helpers, and a validator rejecting duplicate occurrence IDs, dangling parent IDs, and depths inconsistent with the walked parent chain; parentage is an explicit edge only, covered by tests/repositoryManifest.test.ts including the jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external/tmux_lib parent case, and left unwired pending the Phase 4 cutover.

title: Non-destructive refusal of legacy flat repository manifests
description:
Phase 1 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign.

Create scripts/legacyManifest.ts: detect run manifests written by the old flat repository-path model (no manifest version, or a version below the one defined in scripts/repositoryManifest.ts) and mark them incompatible with the new finalizer.

A legacy manifest must never be converted implicitly and must never cause a worktree, branch, or ref to be deleted. Return a refusal result carrying the detected version, the reason, and the exact recovery commands a human can run to finish or unwind that run with the existing tooling.

New module only; no call sites in production code yet.

Tests: a versionless manifest and an older-version manifest are both rejected; the rejection result names the recovery commands; a fixture asserts that after refusal every worktree directory and every ref recorded in that manifest still exists; a current-version manifest passes through untouched.
closureNote: Implemented scripts/legacyManifest.ts refusing versionless and older-version manifests non-destructively, returning the detected version, reason, and recovery commands, with tests asserting worktrees and refs survive refusal and a current-version manifest passes through untouched.

title: Occurrence-graph traversal helpers driven by explicit edges
description:
Phase 1 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign.

Create scripts/repositoryGraph.ts with helpers that operate purely on the manifest edges from scripts/repositoryManifest.ts: direct children of an occurrence, the ancestor chain to the root, deepest-first ordering, the occurrence that owns a given root-relative path, and the path of a file within its owning repository.

Every helper must traverse recorded parent/child edges and recorded depth. None may use dirname(), path-segment removal, slash counting, or longest-prefix matching over raw path strings to infer structure. Ordering must be deterministic — deepest-first, then by path within the immediate parent.

New module only. The equivalent flat-path helpers in scripts/repositoryBranches.ts and scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts stay in place; the Phase 4 cutover task swaps the call sites.

Tests: direct-child lookup, ancestor traversal, ownership, path-within-repository, and deepest-first ordering all verified against a fixture graph containing jfred, jfred/external/tmux_lib, jfred/jfredToolsPlugin, and jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external/tmux_lib; assert the parent of jfred/external/tmux_lib is jfred and that no synthetic path such as jfred/external is ever returned as a repository.
closureNote: Implemented scripts/repositoryGraph.ts traversal helpers driven purely by recorded parent/child edges and depth, with deterministic deepest-first ordering, verified against a fixture graph asserting no synthetic intermediate path is ever returned as a repository.

title: Direct gitlink reader for a parent commit
description:
Phase 1 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign.

Create scripts/gitlinkReader.ts: read every direct gitlink entry from a given repository's commit — the path within that repository and the recorded child OID — using git plumbing (ls-tree of mode 160000 entries) rather than `git submodule foreach`.

Only direct gitlinks of that one repository are returned. A gitlink whose path spans several segments, such as external/tmux_lib, is one direct child of that repository; the intermediate directory is an ordinary tree and must never appear as a repository. The reader must not recurse on its own — recursion is the discovery orchestrator's job.

New module only; no production call sites yet.

Tests: a fixture repo with a gitlink at a single-segment path and one at a multi-segment path returns exactly two direct children with correct OIDs; a repo with no gitlinks returns an empty list; assert intermediate directories are absent from the result; assert a grandchild gitlink inside a child repository is not returned when reading the parent.
closureNote: Implemented scripts/gitlinkReader.ts reading only direct mode-160000 entries via git plumbing, with tests covering single-segment and multi-segment gitlink paths, empty repos, absent intermediate directories, and grandchild gitlinks correctly excluded.

title: Base-branch candidate matching by exact tip OID
description:
Phase 1 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign.

Create scripts/baseBranchResolution.ts: for a repository checked out at a recorded OID, fetch branch refs and return every branch whose tip OID exactly equals that recorded OID. No fuzzy matching, no ancestry checks, no preference for a branch merely because it contains the commit.

The result distinguishes three cases explicitly: exactly one match (usable as baseBranch), zero matches, and multiple matches. Zero and multiple are not errors here — they are returned as candidate sets for the resolution-request module to turn into a question.

New module only; no production call sites yet.

Tests: a repo where exactly one branch tip equals the recorded OID yields that branch as the sole match; a repo where two branches point at the same commit yields both, in deterministic order; a repo where the recorded OID is an ancestor of every branch tip but the tip of none yields zero matches; assert a branch that merely contains the commit is never reported as a match.
closureNote: Implemented scripts/baseBranchResolution.ts matching branches by exact tip OID with distinct single, none, and multiple results; its test file was rewritten from bun:test to the repo node:test convention after the worker worktree lacked node_modules and could not typecheck it.
